contrasts.description: The dental fricatives θ and ð against t, s and d. Spanish θ/d are close but English d is a plosive.
contrasts.label: think / sink

contrasts.description: Voiceless s versus voiced z. Spanish has no z phoneme.
contrasts.label: ice / eyes

contrasts.description: Short ɪ versus long iː. Spanish has one /i/.
contrasts.label: ship / sheep

contrasts.description: Plosive b versus fricative v. Spanish merges them.
contrasts.label: berry / very

contrasts.description: TRAP æ versus STRUT ʌ. Both sit near Spanish /a/.
contrasts.label: cat / cut

contrasts.description: Short versus long back vowels: ɒ/ɔː (cot/caught) and æ/ɑː (cat/cart).
contrasts.label: cot / caught

contrasts.description: Affricate dʒ versus approximant j. Spanish y/ll vary between the two.
contrasts.label: jet / yet

contrasts.description: Final -ed pronounced as a single t or d, present versus absent. Not the extra-syllable ɪd of wanted.
contrasts.label: walk / walked

contrasts.description: Initial h present versus absent. Spanish h is silent.
contrasts.label: eat / heat

contrasts.description: Fricative ʃ versus affricate tʃ. Spanish has only ch.
contrasts.label: ship / chip

contrasts.description: NURSE ɜː versus THOUGHT ɔː; both are spelled with r in ways Spanish reads as o or e.
contrasts.label: work / walk

contrasts.description: Schwa versus a full vowel in an unstressed syllable. Spanish never reduces vowels.
contrasts.label: weak vowel

contrasts.description: Initial s + consonant without a prosthetic e. Production only: no listening pairs.
contrasts.label: school / eschool
